deviation inside it. Chores owns a template of its own,
A name is the user's word for the lane. Renaming never
InProgress to Done makes its tasks count as completed,

This is the archiving act that takes a whole column's
worth at once, on the board in front of the user. The
One request inserts before and after alike. The new
column carries a role from the outset.
Nothing is deleted and nothing is moved.
There is no in-app undo. Recovery is from version
The Backlog column's role is reported as fixed, and a
Done column's as changeable only while another Done
column remains. The user is told what may change
instead of being refused after the fact. An activity-based
project's template governs one board per activity, so the
count says how far any change here reaches.
Every form on this surface drafts as it is filled in, so
leaving it half-finished, a crash and a restart all cost
nothing. The draft is one-way: nothing waits for it to be
kept. Whichever write commits the form discards it.
The role is untouched. Day check-out and the advisor
read the role, never the name.
The Backlog role never changes. The last Done column
cannot leave the role. Within those limits the
Archiving is a conscious gesture here as everywhere: no
task archives itself. This act reaches the one board the
user is on, unlike a change to the template itself.
A task cannot be left without a column, so the cascade is
approve-or-abandon and detaching is not offered.
Deleting a lane deletes it on every board the template
governs, so the disclosure counts all of them. A column
empty everywhere has nothing to disclose and deletes
One Backlog column and at least one Done column,
enforced once per template rather than once per board.
A second Backlog is refused with its reason. The new
lane appears on every board the template governs.
The Backlog column and the last Done column are
refused with their reason, for the same reason their roles
